turns_text: [SEG0001] person_1 (PATIENT): Sorry sorry doctor, we are proper late. The auto got stuck behind a wedding procession near the market, and then this one stopped for coriander. What to do.
[SEG0002] person_2 (DOCTOR): Mm, one second, this screen has hung again. Uh, right, I am with you.
[SEG0003] person_1 (PATIENT): No tension doctor. That coriander fellow was giving a full lecture, rain has spoiled all the mangoes this year, he said.
[SEG0004] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Papa, leave the mangoes na. Let the doctor ask.
[SEG0005] person_2 (DOCTOR): Yes. So what brings you today.
[SEG0006] person_1 (PATIENT): Ah, the thing is, in the mornings I am getting sweating and shaking. Even before my tea.
[SEG0007] person_2 (DOCTOR): Sweating? Sorry, say that once more, I clicked the wrong tab.
[SEG0008] person_1 (PATIENT): Sweating and shaking, doctor. My hands shake like anything. Morning morning it comes.
[SEG0009] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): And breakfast he doesn't touch. Only tea, then the tablet.
[SEG0010] person_1 (PATIENT): Yes, breakfast I am skipping only. One glass tea is plenty. Who is hungry at six.
[SEG0011] person_2 (DOCTOR): Which tablet in the morning? The old file is still not open.
[SEG0012] person_1 (PATIENT): The sugar ones. Glyclazide, and metformine also.
[SEG0013] person_2 (DOCTOR): Gliclazide. The dose, please, I didn't catch it.
[SEG0014] person_1 (PATIENT): Gliclazide eighty mg, one tablet morning. Metformine five hundred mg morning and night, after food. I am diabetic since eight years.
[SEG0015] person_2 (DOCTOR): Right. On the chart it looks a little under-treated. I will increase that morning gliclazide, we will check a urine sugar, and I will see you in one month.
[SEG0016] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Wait, madam. He is swallowing that gliclazide on an empty stomach. And last Tuesday he was confused.
[SEG0017] person_2 (DOCTOR): Confused? Say that again, I was reading the screen.
[SEG0018] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): He was asking where is amma, and amma passed ten years back. Not making sense for maybe twenty minutes. I gave him biscuit and sweet tea and then he was ok.
[SEG0019] person_1 (PATIENT): Oh, that morning, yes. I was not myself. I don't remember the words, but she is correct only.
[SEG0020] person_2 (DOCTOR): Ok. Any chest pain with this sweating and shaking?
[SEG0021] person_1 (PATIENT): No no. Chest is quiet. No pain.
[SEG0022] person_2 (DOCTOR): Breathlessness?
[SEG0023] person_1 (PATIENT): No doctor. Breathing is normal only.
[SEG0024] person_2 (DOCTOR): Any fever, apart from the sweats?
[SEG0025] person_1 (PATIENT): No fever.
[SEG0026] person_2 (DOCTOR): Any allergy to medicines?
[SEG0027] person_1 (PATIENT): Nothing, doctor. No allergy.
[SEG0028] person_4 (NURSE): Sorry doctor, vitals from just now. BP is one thirty two over seventy eight, pulse seventy six, and the finger-prick sugar is sixty four.
[SEG0029] person_2 (DOCTOR): Sixty four. Mm. When did you eat last.
[SEG0030] person_1 (PATIENT): Last night only. Rice and dal, around nine. Morning, nothing, not one biscuit.
[SEG0031] person_2 (DOCTOR): And the morning sweating, since when exactly?
[SEG0032] person_1 (PATIENT): Umm, about three weeks. Well, actually I thought it was after the wedding, no, three weeks only. Most mornings. Sunday if she makes upma, then it is less.
[SEG0033] person_1 (PATIENT): Also err, last year at the camp they checked the sugar. They said it was borderline only. I have not brought that paper.
[SEG0034] person_2 (DOCTOR): So they called an old camp sugar borderline. I will not treat that as a real number.
[SEG0035] person_2 (DOCTOR): I am changing what I said. This looks like low morning sugar from the gliclazide on an empty stomach. No increase, and forget the urine test.
[SEG0036] person_2 (DOCTOR): We will cut the morning gliclazide to forty mg, and you take it only after you have eaten. Metformin stays five hundred mg twice a day with meals.
[SEG0037] person_1 (PATIENT): Forty, ok doctor. I was worried you will add one more tablet. My neighbour said stop everything and drink karela juice, I told him no.
[SEG0038] person_2 (DOCTOR): Good. Do not stop them, and no juice cure. Kindly do not skip breakfast. Even two biscuits before the tablet.
[SEG0039] person_2 (DOCTOR): I will book a fasting blood sugar and an HbA1c. Blood test, not urine. Tomorrow morning, fasting. Reception will give the slip.
[SEG0040] person_1 (PATIENT): Tomorrow, not today? I already didn't eat, but it is late now, what to do.
[SEG0041] person_2 (DOCTOR): Not today, you have been walking about, so tomorrow morning. Come back in two weeks with the report, not one month. I want you sooner after that confusion.
[SEG0042] person_1 (PATIENT): Two weeks, done. Should I bring the old camp paper also if I find it under the bed?
[SEG0043] person_2 (DOCTOR): If you find it, bring it, but we are not waiting on it. If the sweating and shaking comes again, take some sugar, sit down, and call your daughter.
[SEG0044] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): I will see that he eats, madam. I will bring him in two weeks.
[SEG0045] person_2 (DOCTOR): Right. That is the plan. You can go, the forms will be at the desk.

spec.situation: Older diabetic on gliclazide and metformin with morning sweating and shakiness; skips breakfast; daughter reports confusion once; doctor reviews doses and plans a blood test.

traps.happens: The conversation OPENS with a remark, joke, apology for being late, small talk, or a trigger event (a relative's diagnosis, a neighbour's advice, the receptionist's note) BEFORE the real reason is stated. The patient states the real concern a few turns later.
traps.label_rule: chief_complaint is the real concern in a short phrase in the patient's wording (e.g. 'worried about diabetes', 'voice gets tired'). NOT the opening remark, the joke or the trigger (the relative's illness goes into family_history only if it is a relative's condition said as such).

features: doctor_changes_mind: the doctor says one plan, then changes it after new information; the label holds the final plan.
test_result_recalled: the patient reports an old test or result ('they said it was borderline'); recorded as reported history/investigation only as far as said, not as a confirmed value.
spec.doctor_style: distracted by the computer, asks for repeats

bad.reason: Dose and twice-daily use supported; 'with meals' not stated for current regimen, only 'after food'.
bad.text: metformin (dose=500 mg, frequency=twice daily with meals, indication=diabetes, status=currently_used, reported_by=patient)

bad.reason: Doctor continues metformin 500 mg twice daily with meals; responsible person is doctor, not patient.
bad.text: Continue metformin 500 mg twice daily with meals (action_type=counselling, status=recommended, responsible_person=patient)

omissions.text: Current metformin use was stated as 500 mg morning and night after food; the recorded current medication entry omits the 'after food' administration detail.

The current gliclazide was being taken on an empty stomach before breakfast/with only tea, which was central to the assessment of hypoglycaemia and is not recorded as part of the current medication use.
The confusion episode improved after biscuit and sweet tea, and the patient himself said he did not remember the words / was not himself; this corroboration from the patient is not recorded.

The patient had eaten last at about 9 pm the previous night (rice and dal) and had nothing at all that morning, not even one biscuit; this timing/detail related to the low sugar episode is not recorded.

The doctor explicitly cancelled the earlier plan to increase gliclazide, cancelled the urine sugar test, and said to do blood tests instead; the reversal/cancellation of the initial plan is not recorded.
Follow-up was changed from one month to two weeks because the doctor wanted to review him sooner after the confusion episode; the reason for expedited follow-up is not recorded.
